contract.proves:
A node re-entering a cluster while still holding state from a PREVIOUS
membership must reach a terminal outcome inside the install budget — joined,
or failed with a diagnosis. It must never wait forever.

WHY THIS EXISTS. On 2026-08-19 a Day-0 install was run on a machine whose
ScyllaDB data directory still held the previous cluster's Raft group0: five
voters, four of them long gone. The install reached

  "Waiting for ScyllaDB write readiness (DDL probe) on 10.0.0.63:9042..."

and stopped there. CREATE KEYSPACE is a schema change, schema changes take a
group0 read barrier, and a barrier needs 3 of 5 voters. One was alive. The
probe could never succeed, and nothing bounded it: install-day0.sh advertises
a 120s budget as `for _i in $(seq 1 60)` with `sleep 2`, but invokes cqlsh
with no client-side timeout, so a single attempt blocks indefinitely and the
loop never reaches iteration 2. The operator saw one line and no error, for
as long as they were willing to wait.

The four peers were reachable by ICMP but had 9042 and 7000 closed — already
cleaned — so quorum was unrecoverable by restarting them. The install could
not have succeeded; it simply never said so.

THE PROPERTY. Bounded failure, not success. This scenario does not assert
that a dirty node rejoins — that may legitimately be refused. It asserts that
the attempt CONCLUDES, and that the rest of the cluster is not degraded while
it runs. A hang is caught structurally: the bounded wait below expires, the
node has not registered, and the scenario fails on that.

WHY THIS SHAPE OF DIRTY. The node is removed from the cluster and then
restarted WITHOUT wiping its state volume, so its persisted identity and
membership refer to a cluster that no longer lists it. That is the same class
of state as the incident — local evidence of a membership the cluster has
moved past — reachable with existing primitives.

RELATIONSHIP TO first-join-from-clean-node. That scenario proves the CLEAN
path works: detach, remove, WIPE, restart, rejoin. This one is deliberately
the same sequence with the wipe removed, so a diff between the two isolates
exactly one variable: whether prior state was cleared. Passing clean while
hanging dirty is the defect, and only the pair can show it.

NOT COVERED HERE: the cqlsh timeout itself. Reproducing the original hang
needs a ScyllaDB whose group0 cannot reach quorum, which a healthy sim
cluster does not offer without building a foreign ring first. This pins the
boundedness property that the missing timeout violated, at the layer the
harness can actually drive.
